name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.lteNorm
source: ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (u : ℤ_[l]) (c : ℕ), IsLevel l u c → ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ (l : ℤ_[l]) ∣ u - 1 ∧
have hunit : IsUnit u := PadicInt.isUnit_iff.2 hu
have hvmem : v ∈ abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l] := by
set n : ℤ := ((l ^ j * a : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((l ^ j * b : ℕ) : ℤ) with hndef
have hlm : (l : ℤ_[l]) ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[l] := by
have hptU : IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] ↑(abelian₂.pt U) = c := by
rw [show ((U : ℤ_[l]ˣ) : ℤ_[l]) = u from hvu]
rcases Nat.lt_or_ge l 3 with h | h
have key := abelian₂.lte ℤ_[l] l Fact.out hlm U hcond n
have hfac : (u ^ l ^ j) ^ a - (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b = (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b * ↑(abelian₂.pt (U ^ n)) := by
have h1 : ((U ^ n : abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l]) : ℤ_[l]ˣ) = v ^ n := rfl
have h2 : v ^ ((l ^ j * a : ℕ) : ℤ) = v ^ ((l ^ j * b : ℕ) : ℤ) * v ^ n := by
have h3 : ∀ k : ℕ, (u ^ l ^ j) ^ k = ((v ^ ((l ^ j * k : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℤ_[l]ˣ) : ℤ_[l]) := by
rw [h1, h3 a, h3 b, h2, Units.val_mul]
rw [hfac, norm_mul, norm_pow, norm_pow, hu, one_pow, one_pow, one_mul]
· have hcast : ((n : ℤ) : ℤ_[l]) = (l : ℤ_[l]) ^ j * ((a : ℤ_[l]) - (b : ℤ_[l])) := by
show: Let the prime ℓ and the ℓ-adic integer u satisfy the level-c condition. Then u has norm one and u−1 is divisible by ℓ. For all natural j, a and b, the distance between the a-th and b-th powers of u raised to ℓʲ is ℓ to the power −(j+c) times the distance between a and b in the ℓ-adic integers.
strategy: Apply the lifting-the-exponent identity in the group of principal units. Factoring out a norm-one power of u leaves a principal-unit displacement whose valuation gives the exact scale.

steps.claim: The level condition gives $v_\ell(u-1)=c<\infty$, $c\ge1$, and $c\ge2$ when $\ell=2$. Here $v_\ell(0)=\infty$ and the norm has $\lVert\ell\rVert=\ell^{-1}$.
steps.snippet:
∀ j a b : ℕ, ‖(u ^ l ^ j) ^ a - (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b‖ = ((l : ℝ) ^ (j + c))⁻¹ * ‖(a : ℤ_[l]) - b‖ := by
  intro l _ u c hc
  obtain ⟨hv, hc1, hc2⟩ := hc

steps.claim: The prime $\ell$ is a uniformizer of $\mathbf Z_\ell$, so its normalized additive valuation is $1$.
steps.snippet:
have hval1 : IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] (l : ℤ_[l]) = 1 :=
    IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_uniformizer PadicInt.irreducible_p

have hl : (l : ℤ_[l]) ∣ u - 1 := by
    rw [← IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_le_iff_dvd, hval1]
    simp only [vl] at hv
    rw [hv]
    exact_mod_cast hc1

steps.claim: The norm criterion for divisibility by the uniformizer gives $\lVert u-1\rVert<1$.
The inequality $\lVert u-1\rVert<1=\lVert-1\rVert$ implies $\lVert u\rVert=1$ by the ultrametric norm law.
steps.snippet:
have hu : ‖u‖ = 1 := by
    have := PadicInt.norm_eq_of_norm_add_lt_right (z1 := u) (z2 := -1)
      (by rw [norm_neg, norm_one, ← sub_eq_add_neg]; exact hn1)
    rwa [norm_neg, norm_one] at this

steps.claim: We have $\lVert u\rVert=1$ and $\ell\mid u-1$. For arbitrary natural $j,a,b$ the two powers under comparison have exponents $\ell^j a$ and $\ell^j b$ by the power-of-a-power identity.
steps.snippet:
refine ⟨hu, hl, ?_⟩
  intro j a b

steps.claim: An $\ell$-adic integer of norm one is a unit, so $u$ has an inverse in $\mathbf Z_\ell$.
steps.snippet: have hunit : IsUnit u := PadicInt.isUnit_iff.2 hu

steps.claim: Let $v\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ be the unit represented by $u$. Working in the unit group gives meaning to negative integer powers.
The underlying $\ell$-adic integer of $v$ is $u$ by the choice of the unit.
The unit $v$ is a principal unit, since its displacement $u-1$ lies in the maximal ideal of $\mathbf Z_\ell$.
steps.snippet: have hvmem : v ∈ abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l] := by

children.claim: Membership in the principal-unit subgroup means exactly $v-1\in\mathfrak m_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ after viewing $v$ as a ring element.
Maximal-ideal membership is equivalent here to $\lVert v-1\rVert<1$. This follows from $v=u$ in the ring and the established inequality for $u-1$.

steps.claim: Write $U$ for $v$ in the principal-unit subgroup. Set $n=\ell^j a-\ell^j b$ in $\mathbf Z$, so powers of $U$ by $n$ also cover $a<b$ and $a=b$.
steps.snippet:
let U : abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l] := ⟨v, hvmem⟩
  set n : ℤ := ((l ^ j * a : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((l ^ j * b : ℕ) : ℤ) with hndef

steps.claim: The prime $\ell$ is in the maximal ideal because its norm is $\ell^{-1}<1$.
steps.snippet:
have hlm : (l : ℤ_[l]) ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ℤ_[l] := by
    rw [IsLocalRing.mem_maximalIdeal, PadicInt.mem_nonunits, PadicInt.norm_p]
    exact inv_lt_one_of_one_lt₀ (by exact_mod_cast (Fact.out : l.Prime).one_lt)

steps.claim: The displacement $U-1$ has valuation $c$, since its underlying ring element is $u-1$.
steps.snippet: have hptU : IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] ↑(abelian₂.pt U) = c := by

children.claim: The point attached to $U$ is the element $U-1$ of the maximal ideal. Thus its ring valuation is computed on the underlying ring element of $U$ minus $1$.
The underlying ring element of $U$ is $u$, so the displacement in this valuation is precisely $u-1$.
children.snippet: rw [show ((U : ℤ_[l]ˣ) : ℤ_[l]) = u from hvu]

children.claim: The ring element obtained from the principal unit $U$ through the unit group is $u$, by the choice of $v$.
children.snippet: rw [show ((U : ℤ_[l]ˣ) : ℤ_[l]) = u from hvu]

children.claim: Consequently $v_\ell(U-1)=v_\ell(u-1)=c$ by the level condition.

steps.claim: The strict threshold for lifting exponents is $v_\ell(\ell)<(\ell-1)v_\ell(U-1)$. Its left side is $1$, and the level assumptions make $(\ell-1)c>1$.
steps.snippet:
have hcond : IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] (l : ℤ_[l]) <
      ↑(l - 1) * IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] ↑(abelian₂.pt U) := by
steps.typedFact:
IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] (l : ℤ_[l]) <
      ↑(l - 1) * IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] ↑(abelian₂.pt U)

children.claim: Inserting $v_\ell(\ell)=1$ and $v_\ell(U-1)=c$ gives the numerical inequality $1<(\ell-1)c$.
The numerical threshold $1<(\ell-1)c$ holds. At $\ell=2$ it follows from $c\ge2$, and for $\ell\ge3$ it follows from $\ell-1\ge2$ and $c\ge1$.
Every prime is at least $2$, so a prime strictly below $3$ must equal $2$.
The alternatives $\ell<3$ and $\ell\ge3$ distinguish the case needing $c\ge2$ from the case $\ell-1\ge2$.
children.snippet: rcases Nat.lt_or_ge l 3 with h | h

children.claim: If $\ell<3$, primality gives $\ell=2$. The exceptional level condition yields $1<c=(\ell-1)c$.
A prime satisfies $2\le\ell$, so the additional inequality $\ell<3$ forces $\ell=2$.
Substituting $\ell=2$ turns $(\ell-1)c$ into $c$, and the stronger level bound $c\ge2$ makes it strictly bigger than $1$.
children.snippet:
have := hc2 h2
        subst h2
        omega

children.claim: If $\ell\ge3$ then $\ell-1\ge2$. As $c\ge1$, the product $(\ell-1)c$ is at least $2$ and exceeds $1$.
Subtracting one from the bound $\ell\ge3$ gives $\ell-1\ge2$.
The inequalities $\ell-1\ge2$ and $c\ge1$ give $1<2\cdot1\le(\ell-1)c$ by monotonicity of multiplication on natural numbers.
children.snippet:
calc 1 < 2 * 1 := by norm_num
          _ ≤ (l - 1) * c := Nat.mul_le_mul h3 hc1

children.claim: The inequality $1<(\ell-1)c$ holds also in $\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$. Since $v_\ell(\ell)=1$ and $v_\ell(U-1)=c$, it gives the strict bound $v_\ell(\ell)<(\ell-1)v_\ell(U-1)$.

steps.claim: Lifting the exponent for the principal unit $U$ at the signed integer $n$ gives $v_\ell(U^n-1)=v_\ell(U-1)+v_\ell(n)$ under this threshold, also at $n=0$ with value $\infty$.
steps.snippet: have key := abelian₂.lte ℤ_[l] l Fact.out hlm U hcond n

steps.claim: The difference $u^{\ell^j a}-u^{\ell^j b}$ factors as $u^{\ell^j b}(U^n-1)$ because $\ell^j a=\ell^j b+n$ in $\mathbf Z$.
steps.snippet: have hfac : (u ^ l ^ j) ^ a - (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b = (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b * ↑(abelian₂.pt (U ^ n)) := by
steps.typedFact: (u ^ l ^ j) ^ a - (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b = (u ^ l ^ j) ^ b * ↑(abelian₂.pt (U ^ n))

children.claim: Let $w$ be the ring element underlying the principal unit $U^n$. Its attached point has ring value $w-1$, so the second factor in the difference-of-powers formula is $w-1$. Multiplication by the first factor gives $u^{\ell^j b}w-u^{\ell^j b}$.
The underlying unit of the principal unit $U^n$ is $v^n$, since taking integer powers in the subgroup agrees with the ambient unit group.
children.snippet: have h1 : ((U ^ n : abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l]) : ℤ_[l]ˣ) = v ^ n := rfl
children.typedFact: ((U ^ n : abelian₂.oneUnits ℤ_[l]) : ℤ_[l]ˣ) = v ^ n

children.claim: In the unit group $v^{\ell^j a}=v^{\ell^j b}v^n$, by addition of integer exponents.
children.snippet:
have h2 : v ^ ((l ^ j * a : ℕ) : ℤ) = v ^ ((l ^ j * b : ℕ) : ℤ) * v ^ n := by
      rw [← zpow_add]
      congr 1
      rw [hndef]
      ring
children.typedFact: v ^ ((l ^ j * a : ℕ) : ℤ) = v ^ ((l ^ j * b : ℕ) : ℤ) * v ^ n

children.claim: For natural $k$, $(u^{\ell^j})^k$ is the underlying ring element of $v^{\ell^j k}$, since nonnegative integer powers agree with natural powers and multiplication of the exponents composes powers.
children.snippet:
have h3 : ∀ k : ℕ, (u ^ l ^ j) ^ k = ((v ^ ((l ^ j * k : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℤ_[l]ˣ) : ℤ_[l]) := by
      intro k
      rw [zpow_natCast, Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val, hvu, pow_mul]

children.claim: For $B$ the ring image of $v^{\ell^j b}$ and $C$ that of $v^n$, the difference of powers is $BC-B=B(C-1)$. Since $C-1$ is the displacement of $U^n$, this gives the required factorization.
children.snippet:
rw [h1, h3 a, h3 b, h2, Units.val_mul]
    ring

steps.claim: Taking norms of the factorization drops $u^{\ell^j b}$, whose norm is $1$, leaving the norm of $U^n-1$.
steps.snippet: rw [hfac, norm_mul, norm_pow, norm_pow, hu, one_pow, one_pow, one_mul]

steps.claim: Here $a-b$ is the difference of the images of $a$ and $b$ in $\mathbf Z_\ell$. The elements $U^n-1$ and $\ell^{j+c}(a-b)$ have the same extended valuation $j+c+v_\ell(a-b)$, hence equal norms. When $a=b$, both elements are zero.

children.claim: The comparison product has norm $\ell^{-(j+c)}\lVert a-b\rVert$, by multiplicativity and $\lVert\ell^{j+c}\rVert=\ell^{-(j+c)}$.

Both $U^n-1$ and $\ell^{j+c}(a-b)$ have valuation $j+c+v_\ell(a-b)$. This follows from lifting the exponent for the first element, from additivity on products for the second, and from $n=\ell^j(a-b)$. At $a=b$ the common value is infinite.
children.snippet: · have hcast : ((n : ℤ) : ℤ_[l]) = (l : ℤ_[l]) ^ j * ((a : ℤ_[l]) - (b : ℤ_[l])) := by

children.claim: The image of the signed integer $n$ in $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is $\ell^j(a-b)$ because the embeddings preserve subtraction, natural powers and products.
children.snippet:
· have hcast : ((n : ℤ) : ℤ_[l]) = (l : ℤ_[l]) ^ j * ((a : ℤ_[l]) - (b : ℤ_[l])) := by
      rw [hndef]
      push_cast
      ring

children.claim: Lifting gives $v_\ell(U^n-1)=c+v_\ell(n)=c+j+v_\ell(a-b)$. Additivity and $v_\ell(\ell)=1$ give $v_\ell(\ell^{j+c}(a-b))=j+c+v_\ell(a-b)$, the same extended value even when $a=b$.
children.snippet:
rw [key, hptU, hcast, IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_mul, IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_pow,
      IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_mul, IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal_pow, hval1]
    simp only [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    push_cast
    ring

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
